title: TV Trailers of the Week: Criminal, Bad Monkey: S2, Yellowjackets: S4, Percy Jackson and the Olympians: S3, Trinity, Blue Eye Samurai: S2 and More

TV Trailers of the Week: Criminal, Bad Monkey: S2, Yellowjackets: S4, Percy Jackson and the Olympians: S3, Trinity, Blue Eye Samurai: S2 and More 
 Subscribe Sign in TV Trailers of the Week TV Trailers of the Week: Criminal, Bad Monkey: S2, Yellowjackets: S4, Percy Jackson and the Olympians: S3, Trinity, Blue Eye Samurai: S2 and More
 📺 Take a peek at some of the latest trailers for upcoming TV shows.
 TheMovieBox Nov 08, 2026 2 1 Share 📺 “Criminal” Teaser: Charlie Hunnam, Luke Evans, Emilia Clarke, and Adria Arjona Lead Amazon’s Gritty Crime Thriller Based on Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips’ Acclaimed Comics — Part One: “Coward” Premieres Wednesday, January 13th, Followed by Part Two: “Lawless” on January 27th 
 We’re not gonna lie. For a while there, it seemed like Charlie Hunnam might never top the success he had with Sons of Anarchy , let alone recover from the box-office bomb that was King Arthur: Legend of the Sword . 
 But after recent Emmy and Golden Globe nominations for his work on Monster: The Ed Gein Story , it certainly seems like Hunnam is back in full force. And now he’s returning to the world of outlaw crime thrillers with his latest series, Criminal , an adaptation of the acclaimed graphic novels by comic book writer Ed Brubaker and artist Sean Phillips. 
 Hunnam is also part of a pretty impressive ensemble cast that includes Adria Arjona, Emilia Clarke, Luke Evans, Richard Jenkins, Logan Browning, John Hawkes, Patrick J. Adams, Kadeem Hardison and Garrett Hedlund, making this one series to definitely keep an eye on.
 Brubaker himself is serving as co-showrunner, writer, and executive producer alongside crime novelist Jordan Harper ( She Rides Shotgun ), bringing his gritty crime comics to life in an eight-episode series split into two parts, subtitled Coward and Lawless . 
 Each part consists of four episodes, with directing duo Anna Boden and Ryan Fleck ( Captain Marvel , Freaky Tales ) helming Coward , while Dee Rees ( Mudbound ) takes over the directing reins for Lawless . 
 Set to be released just two weeks apart in January, Criminal: Coward will see Hunnam playing Leo Patterson, a cautious thief who’s spent his life trying to stay one step ahead of trouble, only to find himself pulled into a dangerous heist involving his childhood friend and fellow criminal Ricky Lawless, played by Gus Halper ( Unabomber , The Shards ). 
 Meanwhile, Part Two, Lawless , will have Luke Evans taking center stage as Tracy Lawless, Ricky’s older brother, who returns from the Army only to find himself pulled right back into the criminal underworld he left behind when his brother gets caught up in a dangerous situation. 
 Both storylines will be interconnected, and knowing Ed Brubaker, a writer who’s earned quite a reputation for his gritty noir storytelling, we can probably expect plenty of double-crosses, morally questionable characters, and more than a few twists by the end of it all.
 📺 “Bad Monkey: Season 2” Trailer: Vince Vaughn Returns as the Wisecracking Florida Gumshoe, Facing Off Against John Malkovich and a Whole New Cast of Criminal Oddballs in Apple TV’s Offbeat Crime Comedy — Premiering Wednesday, December 2nd on Apple TV 
 What makes someone lucky? Is it someone who’s never had to deal with any real hardship, or someone who’s managed to survive every obstacle life has thrown at them?
 Just something to think about as Vince Vaughn returns as Andrew Yancy, the perpetually unlucky (or extremely lucky, depending on how you look at it) former Miami detective turned health inspector turned laid-back gumshoe who constantly finds himself in a whole lot of trouble. And even more so in season two of Apple TV’s Bad Monkey , from Scrubs , Ted Lasso , and Shrinking creator Bill Lawrence. 
 Based on the bestselling novel by Carl Hiaasen, the series follows Vaughn’s Andrew Yancy, a lowly Florida health inspector who just can’t seem to stay out of murder investigations, especially when there’s a chance he might finally get his detective badge back.
 This time around, Yancy finds himself caught up in another dangerous case, one that puts him in the crosshairs of a powerful and ruthless mob boss played by none other than John Malkovich.
 And as Yancy tries to talk his way out of just about every bad situation he finds himself in, mostly failing miserably, he ends up being targeted by Malkovich and his goons, even finding himself held at gunpoint on a rooftop with little hope of getting out of it unscathed.
 But somehow, Yancy always finds a way to smooth-talk his way off the ledge and live to see another day, proving it never hurts to have the gift of gab.
 With returning cast members Natalie Martinez and John Ortiz, alongside newcomers John Malkovich, Yvonne Strahovski, Sofia Boutella, Charlotte Lawrence, Caleb Landry Jones, Dax Shepard, Mo Amer, and Keyla Monterroso Mejia, season two is shaping up to be another wild and crazy ride through Florida’s wonderfully weird criminal underbelly when it premieres this December on Apple TV.
 📺 “Yellowjackets: Season 4” Trailer: Melanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, Sophie Nélisse, Jasmin Savoy Brown, Sophie Thatcher and the Rest of the Surviving Cast Return for One Final Season of Twisted Secrets, Psychological Horror, and ’90s Nostalgia — Premiering Friday, November 20th on Paramount+ Premium 
 It’s the question everyone wants answered: How did the WHS Yellowjackets return to school after surviving all those months stranded in the wilderness, especially after everything they did just to stay alive? And more importantly, how did these girls manage to keep the horrifying truth about what happened out there a secret for years?
 Season 4 of the hit Showtime series Yellowjackets will mark its final chapter when it returns later this month. Which likely means we might finally get some answers to the biggest mysteries that have been haunting us since we first got hooked back in Season 1. 
 With returning cast members Melanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, Tawny Cypress, Sophie Nélisse, Jasmin Savoy Brown, Samantha Hanratty, Sophie Thatcher, and Courtney Eaton, this timeline-jumping thriller may have started out as the only reason to keep your Showtime subscription active, but now it returns to close out one of television’s most twisted survival mysteries.
 It’s Lost meets Mean Girls meets Lord of the Flies . And it’s been one of those watercooler shows for years now, the kind you just can’t stop texting your friends about. 
 And let’s not forget, Yellowjackets was also one of the first shows to really tap into that emerging wave of ’90s nostalgia, mixing the music, fashion, and teenage angst of the decade with some seriously disturbing psychological horror. 
 So cue the ’90s grunge music, surprise murders, sinister mind games, and enough buried secrets to make you wonder if these girls ever really escaped the wilderness, or if they just brought the horrors of it back home with them.
 📺 “Percy Jackson and the Olympians: Season 3” Trailer: Walker Scobell Returns for Another Dangerous Quest Alongside Tamara Smart, Dafne Keen, and More — Premiering Friday, November 20th on Disney+ 
 Disney has taken an interesting approach to promoting its small-screen adaptation of Rick Riordan’s Percy Jackson and the Olympians . Now heading into its third season, the fantasy adventure series has also found a wider audience thanks to Disney’s deal with Netflix. And so far, that gamble appears to have paid off, with the first two seasons proving popular on Netflix and helping build an even bigger fan base. With excitement growing for the upcoming season, it looks like we’re in for the show’s most action-packed adventure yet. 
 Walker Scobell once again returns as Percy Jackson, the young demigod who finds himself on another dangerous quest, this time to rescue his friend Annabeth Chase (Leah Sava’ Jeffries) from the forces of Kronos. Percy, the son of Poseidon, will be joining forces with Thalia Grace (Tamara Smart), the daughter of Zeus, as they set out to rescue Annabeth and confront a dangerous prophecy that threatens the future of Olympus.
 Also joining the cast this season are a few familiar faces, including Logan star Dafne Keen as Artemis, alongside Kate McKinnon as Aphrodite, Ming-Na Wen as Hera, and Andra Day as Athena. With showrunners Jonathan E. Steinberg and Dan Shotz also returning, this third season will adapt The Titan’s Curse , the third book in Riordan’s popular fantasy series. 
 Set to premiere in just a couple of weeks, there’s still time to catch up on the first two seasons, now streaming on Disney+ and Netflix.
 📺 “Trinity” Trailer: Gugu Mbatha-Raw and Richard Madden Star in Netflix’s Nuclear Conspiracy Thriller Series from “Bodyguard” Creator Jed Mercurio, Also Starring Marcia Gay Harden and Bruce Greenwood — Premiering Tuesday, December 1st on Netflix 
 Cold War-era nuclear threats have inspired some pretty tightly wound thrillers over the years. We can all think of a few classics involving government conspiracies, nuclear missiles, and the possibility of Armageddon. But nowadays, does that kind of thriller still work? Or does it feel a little too old-fashioned?
 Here’s the thing. What makes these thrillers timeless is usually the acting. Give us a stellar ensemble playing out some incredibly tense scenarios, and you’ve got yourself some good, old-fashioned entertainment.
 And that seems to be the case with this new Netflix thriller, Trinity starring Gugu Mbatha-Raw and Richard Madden, alongside Kirk Acevedo, James Remar, Mark O’Brien, Anthony Edwards, Bruce Greenwood, and Oscar winner Marcia Gay Harden. 
 Created by Jed Mercurio, the man behind Line of Duty and Bodyguard , this Netflix original series (out in Dec.) follows a Navy commander (Mbatha-Raw) whose close encounter with a nuclear catastrophe brings her into the inner circle of the U.S. secretary of defense (Madden). Soon, she uncovers a dangerous web of political conspiracies and classified secrets that could push the country toward nuclear disaster. 
 So expect plenty of clenched faces, people screaming “Fire the missiles!” and folks in suits talking out of the sides of their mouths in secret rooms. Because when it comes to a political thriller like this, the most entertaining part is trying to figure out who’s telling the truth, who’s pulling the strings, and who’s about to stab someone in the back... and, more importantly, who the hell is pushing us toward nuclear war? Perhaps someone who needs to be impeached ASAP.
 📺 “Blue Eye Samurai: Season 2” Teaser: Maya Erskine Returns as Mizu, Taking Her Bloody Quest for Revenge to 17th-Century London — Premiering Tuesday, January 19th on Netflix 
 So, you’re not a big anime fan? Well, maybe this Netflix series could be your gateway into the genre. And sure, some hardcore anime fans out there might argue that it’s a bastardized Hollywood version of the art form, but chill out and relax. It could be that starter show for someone looking to break into the wider world of anime.
 After all, Blue Eye Samurai is coming back in January for a second season following its Emmy-winning debut in 2023. And yes, it’s been a few years, and fans have been patiently waiting for its return. Well, the wait is almost over. 
 For the uninitiated, the show features the voices of Maya Erskine as Mizu, a mixed-race swordmaster on a relentless quest for revenge, alongside Brenda Song as Akemi, Darren Barnet as Taigen, and Masi Oka as Ringo.
 Mixing Japanese samurai traditions with the Western archetype of the lone hero, the Netflix series, created by Amber Noizumi and screenwriter Michael Green ( Logan , Blade Runner 2049 ), follows Mizu on a bloody quest that takes her from the streets of feudal Japan to the unfamiliar world of 17th-century London. There, she seeks to track down the two remaining men who may hold the key to her parentage. 
 The first season was hailed by critics as one of the best animated series of 2023. So, naturally, Season 2 comes with plenty of anticipation and some pretty high expectations. It’s set to premiere January 19th on Netflix.
 📺 “Unaccustomed Earth” Trailer: Freida Pinto and Siddharth Star in Netflix’s Multigenerational Family Drama About Love and Regret, Based on Jhumpa Lahiri’s Bestselling Short-Story Collection — Premieres Thursday, December 17th on Netflix 
 Jhumpa Lahiri’s bestselling short-story collection, which tells a multigenerational story of love, family, and cultural identity, provides the basis for this new Netflix drama series from producers John Wells ( ER , The Pitt ) and Madhuri Shekar ( 3 Body Problem ). Featuring a large ensemble cast of mostly South Asian actors, including Slumdog Millionaire’s Freida Pinto, Siddharth, Indraneil Sengupta, Never Have I Ever’s Sarayu Blue, and Manifest’s Parveen Kaur along with The Hangover’s Justin Bartha, the drama revolves around an Indian American family whose lives are turned upside down when a life-changing cancer diagnosis forces a wife and mother (Pinto) to confront the choices she made years ago, including giving up her first love (Siddharth) to satisfy her father’s wishes. Jumping between timelines, the story explores just how those choices ripple across generations, affecting marriages, relationships, and family loyalties, proving that when it comes to past regrets and roads not taken, the decisions we make (and the consequences we live with) are pretty much universal. 
 📺 “The Rockford Files” Promo Teaser: David Boreanaz Steps Into James Garner’s Shoes as the Wisecracking Private Eye in NBC’s Reboot of the Classic ’70s Detective Series — Premieres Saturday, January 2nd on NBC and Streaming the Next Day on Peacock 
 Anyone over 50 might remember watching, or at least know about, that classic ’70s private-eye series The Rockford Files , starring James Garner. And anyone who grew up watching Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Bones probably already knows that David Boreanaz has a certain je ne sais quoi about him, not unlike what Garner brought to the original role. Which makes this a pretty perfect pairing, with Boreanaz stepping into the role of laid-back P.I. Jim Rockford in this upcoming reboot from producer and showrunner Mike Daniels, whose previous credits include Sons of Anarchy and Shades of Blue . And with Superbad and Adventureland helmer Greg Mottola directing the pilot episode, this new take looks to bring back that old-school charm and wisecracking detective work that made the original series such a TV classic. 
 📺 “Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure” Promo Teaser: Netflix Takes Us Back to 1955 for a New Live-Action Prequel, with a New Town, New Characters, and a Fresh Batch of Supernatural Mysteries — Coming in 2028 
 Netflix ain’t ready to let go of one of its biggest franchises. The streaming giant has released the first video announcement for a new spin-off series set within the Stranger Things universe. Yup, the Upside Down is making a comeback, only this time we’re heading back to the 1950s, long before the strange happenings in Hawkins, Indiana. This live-action prequel will take us to an entirely different town and state: Marion, Nevada, in 1955. Kate Trefry, the playwright and writer best known for her work on Stranger Things and its stage prequel, The First Shadow , will serve as showrunner, co-creating the series alongside the Duffer brothers. But will this new series have any connections to the characters from the original show? As of now, we don’t know. What we do know is that the prequel will introduce a whole new cast of heroes and villains, along with a fresh batch of supernatural mysteries. So, don’t put away those D&D dice just yet. You never know when they might come in handy. 
 📺 “Secret Service” Trailer: Gemma Arterton Uncovers a Russian Conspiracy in a British Political Spy Thriller Co-Starring Rafe Spall, Alex Kingston, and Roger Allam — Premieres Sunday, November 22nd on MGM+ 
 Here’s a wild hot take: British spy stories are better than American ones, and it might just come down to the accents. There’s something about a British accent that makes an already tense situation feel even more intense. Maybe it’s the way characters huddle in a corner, whispering in a way that somehow sounds both distinguished and deceitful. It’s just a theory... something to think about. And perhaps one of the reasons British espionage thrillers seem to be thriving right now. Gemma Arterton (who, yes, has a British accent) can be seen huddling in corners, taking secret phone calls, and looking rather tense as she navigates a dangerous political conspiracy involving the Russians in this new espionage thriller series, which also boasts a stellar ensemble that includes Rafe Spall, Mark Stanley, Amaka Okafor, Alex Kingston, and Roger Allam. Created by Tom Bradby and Jemma Kennedy and based on Bradby’s novel of the same name, this five-part political espionage thriller might just lend further support to our theory about why British spy stories have such a knack for making even the quietest conversations feel dangerous.
 📺 “Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy” Trailer: Snoopy Lands on Santa’s Naughty List in a New Peanuts Christmas Special Featuring Music from John Legend, Kamasi Washington, Leon Bridges, and Laufey — Premiering Friday, November 13th on Apple TV 
 Christmas gives us a great opportunity to gather the family around the TV and spend some quality time together. But when it comes to picking the right show or special, you want something wholesome, something good and honest, something that brings the whole family together. And who better than Snoopy, right? Apple TV is releasing a new holiday special this month featuring Snoopy and the gang. Based on Charles M. Schulz’s classic comic strip Peanuts , this throwback Christmas special finds our beloved beagle on Santa’s naughty list, with just 12 days until Christmas to prove he’s a good dog after all. But if that’s not enough to give you that warm, fuzzy feeling in your belly, you should know that it also features new music from John Legend, Kamasi Washington, Leon Bridges, and Laufey. So ring in the holidays with a few familiar faces, some festive music, and a little Christmas cheer, courtesy of Snoopy, Charlie Brown, and the rest of the Peanuts gang. 
 📺 “A Proud Family Wizmas” Trailer: Penny Proud Takes Over for Santa Claus in a Nostalgic Stop-Motion Christmas Special Featuring the Voices of Kyla Pratt, Tommy Davidson, Paula Jai Parker, and JoMarie Payton — Debuts Saturday, November 14th on Disney+ 
 Remember those classic stop-motion Christmas specials? The ones that told traditional holiday stories through that charming, homemade-looking claymation? There was just something about them that captured the spirit of Christmas and brought back that warm, nostalgic feeling of the holidays. Well, get ready to feel that way again, as The Proud Family , traditionally a 2D animated cartoon, is bringing us a new Christmas special, this time entirely in stop-motion. Featuring the voices of Kyla Pratt, Tommy Davidson, Paula Jai Parker, and JoMarie Payton, this holiday special follows Penny Proud as she reluctantly takes Santa’s place after her complaints about the commercialization of Christmas cause him to quit on Christmas Eve. It’s a clear nod to those classic Rankin/Bass-produced Christmas animated shorts, so prepare to be overloaded with those cozy, fuzzy feelings we got from the holiday specials we grew up watching. 
 🎥 “A Disney Holiday Short: The Invisible Horse” Trailer: ‘Paddington in Peru’ Director Dougal Wilson Brings a Little Christmas Magic to Disney’s Heartwarming Tale of an Unlikely Friendship — Arriving on Disney+ and YouTube November 9th 
 Paddington in Peru director Dougal Wilson has teamed up with Disney for a charming new holiday short about childhood imagination, unlikely friendships, and believing in things you can’t always see. Just when a young boy named Jack begins to think he’s getting too old for Christmas, an unexpected friendship with an invisible horse might be just what he needs to rediscover a little holiday magic. The short will be available on Disney+ and Disney’s YouTube channel next week, giving families a chance to enjoy a little Christmas magic early. Because let’s face it, everyone wants to get into the holiday spirit a little sooner rather than later. 
 📺 “Bobby Lee: Finally” Trailer: After More Than 30 Years in Comedy, the MADtv Veteran and Popular Podcaster Returns to His San Diego Hometown for His First-Ever Stand-Up Special — Premieres Friday, November 27th on Hulu 
 Bobby Lee has been in comedy for more than 30 years. And despite being a longtime cast member of MADtv , it’s taken Bobby quite some time to really make a name for himself. Now a comedy veteran and popular podcaster, he returns to his hometown of San Diego for his first-ever hour-long stand-up special. And it’s a real homecoming, as he returns with an established career and a loyal fan base that has followed him for decades. This time, he brings brutally honest stories and observations about his personal life and family, along with the kind of unpredictable humor that made him such a lovable goofball in the first place. Appropriately titled Finally , Bobby Lee finally puts out his first comedy special, showing us that it’s never too late to accomplish something you’ve always wanted to do. 
 📺 “Nate Bargatze: Good for Nathan” Trailer: The Comedy Superstar Returns With His Fourth Netflix Stand-Up Special, Finding the Funny Side of Everyday Life, Marriage, and Modern Conveniences — Debuts Tuesday, November 24th on Netflix 
 Anyone who’s been following Nate Bargatze’s comedy career will tell you the guy is extremely funny, hardworking, and has a knack for turning everyday nuisances into comedy gold. But even his most die-hard fans might be surprised by just how big a comedy superstar he’s become. At this point, he ranks among the biggest stand-up comedians working today. And now he’s back with yet another Netflix comedy special, proving that sometimes the biggest voice in comedy isn’t the loudest or most obnoxious one in the room, but the one that speaks softly and still manages to bring the house down.
 📺 “Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death” Trailer: Adam McKay-Produced Docuseries Explores the Dark Side of Extreme Body Transformations and Social Media Obsessions — Streams Tuesday, November 10th on Hulu 
 What the hell is looksmaxxing? Is that just some silly slang the kids are throwing around these days? Well, it’s actually a term used to describe a new lifestyle that has emerged in the age of social media. They used to say “sex sells,” but these days, it’s become much more than that. It’s an entire lifestyle built around looks, physical appearance, and creating an almost fictional version of yourself, one that has become increasingly shocking and twisted. In this new three-episode docuseries from executive producer Adam McKay and director Stacey Lee, the world of looksmaxxing comes under the microscope as a group of influencers pushes the limits of physical transformation, with dangerous experiments, bitter rivalries, and a mysterious death raising troubling questions about just how far some are willing to go to look as physically perfect as possible.
 📺 “The Boy Who Stole Billions?” Trailer: New Three-Part Documentary Explores Sam Bankman-Fried’s Meteoric Rise and the Collapse of His $32 Billion Cryptocurrency Empire — Premieres Monday, November 30th on Prime Video 
 Tech bros. Yeah, they’re annoying as hell. But what does it actually mean to be a tech bro? Well, at one time, it meant spoiled, rich, elitist frat dudes. But in reality, some of the most despicable tech bros aren’t necessarily the ones you’d expect. Sometimes, it’s the messy, socially awkward man-child whose intelligence is matched only by his appetite for taking risks. Sam Bankman-Fried might look like your typical awkward, unkempt, harmless tech nerd, but behind that messy hair and unassuming appearance was a man running a sketchy cryptocurrency empire once valued at $32 billion. He has since become the face of one of the biggest financial fraud scandals in modern history. This new three-part docuseries explores the meteoric rise and fall of his cryptocurrency empire, featuring interviews with former insiders and Bankman-Fried himself, speaking from prison about the decisions that led to billions in missing customer funds and his eventual fraud conviction.
 📺 “Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow” Trailer: British Prankster Oobah Butler Takes on the World of Scams, Fake Businesses, and Outrageous Money-Making Schemes in This New Five-Part Docu-Comedy Series — Premiering Sunday, November 22nd on HBO and HBO Max 
 How do you become rich? Better question: How do you get rich in this day and age, when it seems like everyone is trying to sell you some kind of snake oil product? And no matter how outrageous the idea, it’s all about selling you the illusion that something is worth more than it actually is. Well, British satirist, prankster, and filmmaker Oobah Butler gets to the bottom of it in this new HBO docuseries, presenting himself as a potential entrepreneur looking to break into various industries with wild and crazy ideas. Some crazier than others. His goal? To see if anyone will bite on his ridiculous proposals and, in turn, expose just how easily people can be fooled... and just how far some are willing to go to convince themselves of a lie if it means making a quick buck.
 📺 “Fool Night” Trailer: New Netflix Anime Imagines a World Without Sunlight, Where Humans Are Turned Into Plants to Keep Humanity Alive — Streams Thursday, November 26th on Netflix 
 When it comes to anime, world-building is on a whole different level. It’s a genre that comes up with some of the most exciting high-concept stories. Take, for instance, this new Netflix anime series. It’s set in a future where the sun has vanished and Earth is trapped in perpetual darkness. ( Boom. Right there. Great start. ) Humanity has found a disturbing way to survive: turning people into oxygen-producing plants. ( Okay, a little weird. But we’re with you. ) Struggling to support his ailing mother, a desperate young man considers undergoing the procedure himself, only to stumble upon a sinister conspiracy that could expose the terrifying truth behind humanity’s survival. ( Okay, this one might have just climbed to the top of our watch list. ) 
 📺 “The Blue Road” Trailer: Son Sukku and Eita Nagayama Star as Korean and Japanese Detectives Forced to Work Together to Catch a Brutal Serial Killer in Netflix’s Twisty Crime Thriller — Debuts Friday, November 20th on Netflix 
 Historically, Korea and Japan haven’t exactly been on the best of terms. You know, that whole Japanese occupation of Korea that ended after World War II. So, yeah, there’s some long-standing resentment there. We get it. But that history makes for an interesting setup for this new Korean series, which brings both cultures together in what looks to be a deliciously twisty crime thriller. Starring Son Sukku and Eita Nagayama, the series follows two detectives from South Korea and Japan who are forced to work together when a string of brutal murders leaves behind cryptic messages written in each other’s languages. As they try to put aside their cultural differences, they begin to suspect that the murders are connected by something a lot more pernicious than either initially imagined. And catching the killer might require them to confront their own prejudices and learn to trust one another, at least long enough to bring the real culprit to justice.
 📺 “Always on Call” Trailer: Sara Khorami Stars as a Surgeon Thrown Into the Chaos of an Overwhelmed Oslo Emergency Room in Netflix’s New Norwegian Medical Drama — Streams Thursday, November 26th on Netflix 
 Okay, sure, Norway has universal healthcare. But that doesn’t mean its medical dramas are any less intense or filled with fewer heartbreaking stories. After all, no matter what country you’re in, these shows have a way of reminding us what makes us human. It’s our ability to help others and, just as importantly, to ask for help when we’re at our lowest. And that’s what makes this new Netflix series so interesting. It’s The Pitt , minus all that medical debt. The Norwegian drama stars Sara Khorami as a promising but impatient surgeon who finds herself reassigned to an overwhelmed emergency room in Oslo. Between the daily chaos of treating patients, hospital politics, and complicated relationships, balancing her professional ambitions becomes a nearly impossible task. Yet with every patient she manages to help comes the reassurance that she might be exactly where she needs to be. 
 📺 “High Country: Season 2” Trailer: Leah Purcell Returns as Detective Andie Whitford to Investigate a Twisty Double Murder in This Australian Crime Thriller Series — Now Streaming on Hulu 
 One of the big reasons U.S. audiences should give foreign imports a chance is the opportunity to discover new talent from around the world. And that’s certainly the case with this Australian crime thriller, where Leah Purcell finds herself at the center of a twisty murder mystery, playing Detective Andie Whitford, who is called in to investigate a double murder aboard a houseboat on drought-stricken Lake Eildon. Now, Purcell might not be a well-known name here in the States, but she certainly brings a certain gravitas to the role, leading what looks to be a tightly wound crime thriller where her character finds herself caught in an investigation that becomes increasingly personal the deeper she digs into the buried secrets of a small community. And who doesn’t like a good murder mystery where the hero is constantly underestimated, yet only grows more determined to uncover the truth? Crikey!
